title: National Standard for Driving Cars
whatItIs: DVSA's standard for what you need to be a safe and responsible driver of a category B car or light van. It's split into roles, then units, then elements.
keyFacts: Roles split into units; units into elements.
It applies to manual and automatic cat B vehicles, on any road, at any time, in any weather.
'May cause drowsiness' on a medicine means it's highly likely to cause drowsiness.
Whatever the legal limits, it's best to have no alcohol in your system.
Have an eyesight test at least every 2 years: eyesight gets worse over time.
Role 5 values regular driver development sessions with a competent instructor.

a.label: Performance standards
points: What you must be able to do
e.g. scan the driving space, near and far

b.label: Knowledge and understanding
points: What you must know and understand
e.g. what aquaplaning is and when it happens

onTheTest.question: Which role of the National standard for driving cars and light vans covers learning from experience and keeping up to date?
onTheTest.why: Role 5 'Review and adjust driving behaviour over lifetime' has unit 5.1 Learn from experience and unit 5.2 Keep up to date with changes.

onTheTest.question: Congestion makes you stop in a tunnel. What gap does the national standard say to leave to the vehicle in front?
onTheTest.why: Element 4.2.1: if congestion in a tunnel causes you to stop, leave at least a 5 metre gap between you and the vehicle in front.

traps: Eco-safe driving never means reducing safety to improve economy.
Use an emergency roadside telephone rather than a mobile: the operator can find your exact position.
Any alcohol can make you more likely to fall asleep, even below the legal limit.
